main_body: Two-storey half-timbered tavern: a large terracotta tile roof over a plaster front wall with timber frame, shuttered windows, a plank door and a hanging sign
top_band: Roof slope: orange tile rows 1-43 (lightest tiles #f0b070/#e08c48 with darker tile gaps), ending in a dark eave edge around rows 42-44
evidence: The roof reads as a big sloped top surface with per-tile highlights, taking the same role as the roof of the Beodeul house references. Below it the eave casts a dark line onto a vertical plaster wall, rows 44-90. The wall has timber posts and a mid beam. The windows have shutters and sills, and the door has a dark frame and sits set into the wall. A stone plinth sits at the base. No receding side faces are drawn. This matches the reference houses' construction.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have 5-6 orange steps with individual tile highlights. The plaster is speckled in several greys and creams. The outlines are dark brown, tinted to the neighbouring wood and roof (4% neutral dark edge pixels, against 7-9% on the references). Flat-fill coverage is 1%. The median of 16 colours per tile sits between the two references (18 and 11). The 48 distinct colours are fewer than the references' 185 and 66, but the structure and texture hold up well next to them. The piece would sit comfortably beside the references.
